question: Which wastewater plants should Horton call first?
html:
Horton's First Wastewater Calls

Horton should call New Haven East Shore, Hartford and Norwalk first. All three are in Connecticut, Horton's home state, and each has work on the state's fundable list. MWRA Deer Island and Bridgeport Westside come next. (CET wastewater-plant targets; CET growth plan)

1New Haven East Shore STP (40 MGD)98$82M wet-weather and odor-control upgrade, FY27$19.2M process-air compressors
2Hartford WPCF (60 MGD)96$24.3M sludge screening and equalization, FY26-27$31.6M Island Road and Hog Brook pump stations

4MWRA Deer Island94$289M Clarifier #2, in the 2026 state funding plan—

(CET wastewater-plant targets)

Why This Order

  • New Haven has the largest fundable project on the list. It also has a separate compressor request.
  • Hartford is Connecticut's largest plant. Its pump-station requests fit the Phase 3 monitoring and SCADA push in the growth plan (CET growth plan).
  • Norwalk is the best fit for a Horton electrical bid paired with NuWave efficiency work. Aeration is the plant's biggest energy load.
  • Deer Island already generates 26% of its own electricity. The pitch there is electrical subcontracting plus storage and efficiency, not solar.

Signals From EPA Data

  • Permit dates. New Haven's permit expired Feb 28, 2021, and Hartford's expired Sep 30, 2020. Both are administratively continued. Norwalk's permit expired Mar 31, 2026 (CET wastewater-plant targets). Plants with lapsed permits may be planning capital work. That is an inference, not a confirmed link.
  • Bridgeport Westside shows 12 quarters of noncompliance and 1 quarter of significant noncompliance. Its last inspection was Nov 20, 2024 (EPA wastewater-plant compliance).
  • Stamford (24 MGD) is not in the top five shown. It does have an open violation, an expired permit and an inspection on Sep 17, 2026. It may be worth a later screen (EPA wastewater-plant compliance).

Caveats

  • Connecticut Table 3 items are requests that can only draw on first-come reserves. Only Table 2 and Category I items are fundable. Treat the compressor, pump-station and aeration figures as possible future work, not awarded work.
  • The Rhode Island list is a June 2026 draft.
  • Win rates, contract timing and Horton's existing relationships at each plant are not in the context. Bid-history and contact data would be needed to rank call order by likely revenue.

Next Actions

  1. Map Horton's current contacts at the Greater New Haven WPCA, the Metropolitan District Commission and Norwalk. Book first calls before FY27 bid packages are issued.
  2. Get the full Bridgeport Westside rationale from the target file. Confirm the project and dollar value before ranking it against Deer Island.
  3. Build a joint Horton and NuWave pitch for the Norwalk aeration request.
  4. Track which of the 62 projects move from Table 3 to Table 2 in the next state list update.
